character: 5.1km circuit in the Eifel Mountains. Technical first sector (Mercedes Arena), fast cascading second sector, and chicane-hairpin finale. Demands precision in slow sections and commitment in fast ones.
sources: https://www.formula1.com/en/racing/2026/germany/circuit historical F1 GP-circuit corner naming (Castrol-S, Mercedes Arena, Dunlop Kehre, Schumacher S, Veedol, NGK)

corners.name: Castrol-S
corners.technique: Brake at 100m board or start of red-white kerbing. 1st gear, late apex, use all exit road
corners.trap: Misjudging braking on the downhill — easy to over-shoot

corners.name: Mercedes Arena
corners.technique: T2: dab brake at grey kerbing ref, 2nd gear. Stick to inside through T3 as it tightens. T4: flick in early, short-shift to 2nd
corners.trap: T3 keeps tightening — running wide here ruins T4 exit onto the straight

corners.name: Turn 5-6
corners.technique: Smooth direction changes, use inside kerbs. Good exit feeds Dunlop Kehre approach
corners.trap: Over-driving compromises approach to the hairpin

corners.name: Dunlop Kehre
corners.technique: Tricky braking — no clear reference point. Trail brake to early first apex, coast, then get on power for second apex
corners.trap: Misjudging the downhill braking zone; no reference markers make this consistently tricky

corners.name: Schumacher S
corners.technique: High-speed commitment, smooth direction change. Carry speed through both parts
corners.trap: Fighting the car with corrections instead of flowing through

corners.name: Turn 10-11
corners.technique: Good exit from T11 feeds Bit-Kurve and the fast section

corners.name: Veedol
corners.technique: Brake between 100m and 50m, 3rd gear. Cut inside kerb T13, smash inside kerb T14 (if ride height allows)
corners.trap: Hitting concrete block on T13 kerb unsettles the car

corners.name: NGK Chicane
corners.technique: Hard braking, tight hairpin. Clean exit onto start/finish straight
corners.trap: Braking too late and missing the apex; poor exit costs pit straight speed
